payload.goal: UI fixture (hand-written, not a recorded run): audit four mathematical and statistical claims from the DESeq2 methods (Love, Huber & Anders 2014), one of them planted.

payload.title: Moderated estimation of fold change and dispersion for RNA-seq data with DESeq2
payload.excerpt: We model the read count of each gene in each sample with a negative binomial distribution with mean μ and a gene-specific dispersion α, so that the variance of a count is μ + αμ². Gene-wise dispersion estimates are shrunk towards a trend fitted over all genes by their mean, which stabilises them when there are few replicates. To test for differential expression, the estimated log2 fold change is divided by its standard error, and the resulting Wald statistic is compared against a standard normal distribution. P values from the genes that pass independent filtering are adjusted for multiple testing with the procedure of Benjamini and Hochberg, which controls the false discovery rate.

question.text: Is the variance of a negative binomial count with mean μ and dispersion α equal to μ + αμ²?

hypothesis.statement: Var(K) = μ + αμ² exactly: a gamma-Poisson mixture with shape 1/α has this variance.
hypothesis.author: mathematician
hypothesis.rationale: Reading of the methods passage for: Under the negative binomial model, the variance of a count is μ + αμ² (mean μ, dispersion α).

hypothesis.statement: The variance is not μ + αμ²; the quadratic term has another form.
hypothesis.author: statistician
hypothesis.rationale: Reading of the methods passage for: Under the negative binomial model, the variance of a count is μ + αμ² (mean μ, dispersion α).

hypothesis.statement: The variance is μ + μ²/α (α a size parameter), so the formula holds only after inverting α.
